approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs. It keeps the best 64 accepted molecules, samples breeding parents from score-ranked bands, and builds a fresh pool through connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom/bond edits. Aromatic atom exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity checks reject duplicates, and a narrow sulfur rule prevents a new outside-envelope environment from exceeding its maximum count in the actual scored generating parents. A task-local Gaussian process learns from every accepted label using chiral Morgan occurrence counts. It ranks the fresh pool through masked maxima of correlated function draws, then returns accepted offspring to both learning and breeding.
approach.novelty: Replace that active learner and allocation rule with one pairwise Bayesian ranking mechanism: train a small network directly on comparisons between accepted molecules and select with an upper confidence bound in its own latent ranking units. This changes learned weights and acquisition together. Siblings tried frozen contextual predictions with the old GP residual, transformed GP targets, bootstrap-tree draws and diversity-oriented allocation or breeding. This experiment instead learns relative order locally, while retaining the Parent count inputs and graph search. Better ordering could direct evaluations toward larger real parent-beating gains; it is not yet evidence of better endpoints.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting Parent behavior is low productive yield from selected fresh offspring, not failed execution or missing model exposure. Directly reading all three n-1744a1494180 summary.json/run.log pairs gives fifteen successful endpoints, mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878. A read-only recount of its actual per-task candidate logs gives only 648 strict best-generating-parent wins among 4350 accepted offspring, summed positive margin 17.25153528627184, and 255 sequential incumbent advances; every session has a negative mean offspring-minus-best-parent margin. Its mean accepted score is 0.372050 and summed sequential incumbent gain is 5.819415. The late deco_hop seed-0 endpoint 0.8561477222467935 stays in the comparison. This does not prove the GP is misspecified: n-04741f9b1832 removal of its active location loses 0.182967629428378 on the complete matched panel, and count-location/count-residual removals n-161b32768a03/n-b77e5493be1e lose 0.08822718632415433/0.03715967951388403 under their literal conditions. The fully delivered native contextual alternative n-5277bf3b7425 has 435 nonconstant pools, 2834 changed accepted choices and 2510 accepted descendants from 775 changed sources, yet same-label pair accuracy is 0.657184 versus passive GP 0.698242 and Spearman 0.402270 versus 0.505819. Its 654 local wins exceed 648 but positive gain mass falls to 14.377969; mean endpoint delta is -0.07575616042183468 with 13 losses, two gains and higher dispersion. Its recipe ends. The old projected n-3062f0c87203 cross-lock comparison remains unpaired; exact-lock location removal n-fe734eb5c1df supports a negative scoped active-location contribution and reproduces old trajectories, not an independent baseline. Older normal-midrank GP targets n-ae12ccae8c7b, bootstrap-tree allocation n-7922cfd1903a, molecular-encoder location n-61c472c961cc, determinant diversification n-9b90d71cc6e1 and delivered niche breeding n-37a4fc183d94 remain contrary fixed-method results. Earlier protected-record nonuse n-28dc36ed5be7 motivates actual delivery joins, not a new retention intervention. Direct task-local pairwise weight learning plus compatible latent acquisition is a specific unmeasured alternative at this same feedback-ranking question; neither previous breadth nor source-paper efficacy establishes its benefit.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse frozen r35-pairwise-ranking-iterative-review-20261005: its observed bottleneck, current Anchor, accepted-context size, exact lock and one-position conditions still match this immutable task. The inherited queries are the actual Search Policy queries, not new searches claimed by Improve. Improve additionally read the cached pinned model/data/bo/early-stop and Intel sources and opened the primary v1 paper. Adopt one small direct-pair learner plus its own latent UCB, with explicit representation, pool, cadence, learning-rate, tie, stream and local-subset deviations. Existing GP controls justify preserving reference boundaries, not the new method efficacy. The source small-context result supports this test only; de novo productive gain and complete matched endpoints remain unmeasured. The native and projected frozen-context recipes and ordinal GP transform remain stopped, the old pairing limitation persists, and no individual loss/prior/UCB contribution or ranking-mediated cause is identified by this joint contrast.

hypothesis: At each original accepted-archive refit, train a fresh fixed two-hidden-layer Bayesian rank network on uniformly sampled unordered accepted-label pairs with tie-zero, zero-margin ranking loss and source Gaussian KL regularization; replace active GP function-draw allocation by stable masked maxima of the network ten-draw latent mean plus 0.3 times sample standard deviation over the unchanged fresh count-feature pool, keeping the original GP passive.

finding_summary.headline: Pairwise learning changed search but weakened ordering and useful gains
finding_summary.insights: This rules out lack of informative pairs, a wholly collapsed rank output, or failure to deliver changed molecules as explanations for the observed lack of benefit. Local win counts were misleading: the Child offspring faced substantially weaker generating parents, with mean best-parent score 0.243566 versus 0.455304, while mean offspring quality fell to 0.197223 from 0.372050. Broader core discovery also failed to translate into stronger progress: productive typed-core first arrivals increased from 262 to 424, yet their accepted descendants' positive gain fell from 4.289217 to 2.151438. The molecular assessment is consistent with this gap: large repeated aromatic assemblies, crowded cages and uneven local heteroatom chemistry coexist with lower labels than the Parent's more compact alternatives. Those associations do not identify a timeout cause or prove that a size/chemistry filter would help. All seven borrowed elements operated, but the explicit count representation, fresh-pool, cadence, tie, learning-rate and random-stream adaptations limit transfer from the source study. The result applies to the joint fixed learner/UCB recipe; it does not isolate the loss or acquisition, prove ranking-mediated score loss, or refute pairwise learning generally. The missing endpoints prevent a complete performance verdict, but the exposed ordering/productivity failures and 13 completed losses provide no justified continuation or parameter rescue for this recipe.
finding_summary.results: The learner and allocation mechanism ran in all 15 sessions: 421 informative fits produced nonconstant pool means, 3770 of 4210 accepted offspring differed from the passive GP selected set, 3579 changed choices reached informative next-fit training, and 1145 changed parents produced 3427 distinct accepted direct descendants. On the same accepted labels, pair-order accuracy was 0.470128 versus 0.706399 for the passive GP, and mean batch Spearman was -0.074808 versus 0.512550. Both measures were worse in every task/seed aggregate and in each pooled early, middle and late phase; one small middle-phase cell favored the learner. Parent-beating offspring increased from 648 to 801, but summed positive gain fell from 17.251535 to 9.643219 and sequential incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 2.074884. Comparing equal-length Parent prefixes leaves the same adverse direction. All 13 completed task/seed endpoints were lower. The only complete seed macro was 0.303631 versus its matched Parent 0.643098, a delta of -0.339467. Two deco_hop sessions timed out at 190 and 270 observations, so the complete three-seed +0.002 goal and Child dispersion remain unevaluable. Eighteen terminal evaluator labels had saved predictions/provenance but no Candidate offspring receipt; they enter offline ordering and gain measurements, never later-feedback exposure.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich output includes giant aromatic assemblies and halogenated cages; compact plausible alternatives and stereochemical definition remain weak
molecular.overall_character: Node n-ccb8d255bf00 produces highly connected molecular graphs, not a ring-poor fragment collection. Different sessions favor hydrazine/thiocarbonyl polycycles, enormous linked aromatic assemblies, halogenated aryl systems, nitrogen/carbonyl heterocycles, or saturated polyacetal-like cages. The digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9759-1.0. Aromatic-string incidence is 0.931-1.0 in four tasks but only 0.0368 in the saturated-cage task. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are zero throughout; neutral notation does not mean that every nitrogen is nonbasic. Overall structural diversity is moderate because distinct families appear across seeds and tasks, while leading molecules within each session tend to be close relatives. Ring richness is not missing; coherent local chemistry, manageable size and stereochemical definition are inconsistent. All 15 supplied Child and 15 exact accepted archived Parent trajectory paths were present and read. The Child contributes 4360 observations, including 4210 accepted optimizer observations; Parent n-1744a1494180 contributes 4500 observations, including 4350 accepted optimizer observations. Initial molecules and labels match in every corresponding session. These files describe accepted evaluated molecules, not every unscored pool member or rejected proposal. Seed 0 completes all tasks. Seeds 1 and 2 retain all four other completed tasks and respectively 190 and 270 observations of deco_hop, whose evaluator summaries report Objective Session timeouts. Their observed incumbents are not 300-observation endpoints. No missing observations are imputed and no complete three-seed score panel is constructed. context.comparison has child_complete=false, paired_complete=false and only seed 0 as a complete matched seed. The Parent has complete accepted trajectories for all seeds; late Parent improvements remain relevant, including its seed-0 deco_hop change at evaluation 281. Matched-prefix descriptions of the censored streams are distinguished from full Parent endpoints. The operator post-panel seal verification is an identity check, not an evaluator receipt, and neither molecular size nor chemical complexity is asserted to cause a timeout. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 descriptors of the trajectory SMILES support the size, perceived-ring and stereochemical descriptions. RDKit finds unassigned potential tetrahedral centres in 3022 of 4210 Child optimizer observations, compared with 2455 of 4350 Parent observations. These unequal-denominator totals include the censored sessions and are descriptive. Sanitization is not evidence of accessible conformations, synthetic routes or stability. No synthesis, pharmacology, conformer generation or new objective evaluation was performed. Descriptor records, source path hashes and per-session best/worst/final observations are in .slots/L01-resume-20261004/r35-slot0-molecular/chemistry_evidence.json and the adjacent Child/Parent molecule records. cited_smiles contain only Child strings in the immutable request digest or its trusted citation_trajectory_paths; Parent chemistry is described from the separately supplied authoritative Parent trajectories. The frozen catalog v-6e742fd992ff2e91f8cedc44 reports full_history_processed=false and retains unresolved coverage and contribution conditions. This report reads the current Parent molecular assessment through the supplied evidence_index and preserves the older gap provenance it records, rather than claiming an independent review of all earlier histories. Chemical associations do not establish mechanism activation, component contribution, alternative rollout values, or a general benefit from a structural filter. The current partial panel supplies conditional output evidence only.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer observations have a median of 26 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, compared with Parent medians of 24 and three. The seed-0 highest-label molecule is a brominated/chlorinated polycyclic hydrazone carrying a methylurea-like carbonyl linkage; seed 1 favors a methoxy/acetyl-substituted indole-like aromatic thioamide with a fluoropyridyl group and N-S attachment; seed 2 favors a phenolic thiosemicarbazide-like linkage to a densely bridged hydrazone/cyclodiene system. The seed leaders have 25, 26 and 25 heavy atoms and five, three and five perceived rings. There is real aromatic and heterocyclic diversity, but it is often achieved through awkward N-N/S connectivity or additional unsaturated closures. The compact thioamide/aromatic fragments are recognizable; the complete bridged products are questionable synthetic targets. The final seed-0 observation returns to a much larger coupled hydrazone assembly, whereas final seed 1 and seed 2 remain sulfur-rich cyclic relatives.
liabilities: Frequent N-N and N-O connections require local chemical assessment; N-S attachment and hydrazone/thioamide motifs cannot be treated as interchangeable stable amides.

The digest reports cumulated-double-bond text incidence 0.0655. RDKit identifies cumulated carbon double bonds in 57 of 870 optimizer observations; this is distinct from ordinary carbonyl groups or sulfur oxides.

Several leaders contain crowded bridged unsaturation or large nonaromatic unsaturated rings, with unspecified stereochemistry. Tiny fragments and oversized concatenations are both observed low-label extremes.
missing_features: Compact, chemically conventional alternatives to the successful aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are not consistently represented among Child leaders; the stronger Parent azaaryl amide/thione leaders demonstrate that extra bridging is not required in this evidence.
The bridged leaders do not specify their potentially stereogenic centres. The labels do not reveal an exact missing target pharmacophore or prove a stereochemical penalty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Observed best labels for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.4031937733859023 at evaluation 263, 0.40314990987966176 at 164, and 0.4083131679015095 at 284. The corresponding Parent leaders are more compact azaaryl carbonyl/thione arrangements with labels 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Parent seed 0 supplies a relatively conventional halogen-free azaaryl N-hydroxy amide counterexample to requiring the Child halogenated bridged geometry. In the Child, NF and water score 0.0, while a large concatenated aromatic structure at seed 1 evaluation 21 scores 2.3981579588901764e-30; the coupled final seed-0 molecule also falls to 3.668477344274702e-18. In each Child seed the higher-score quartile is smaller by median heavy-atom count than the lower-score quartile. The visible reward is an intermediate-sized complete heteroatom/aromatic arrangement, not added aromatic mass, hydrazine content or halogens alone. The final emitted molecule is not necessarily the incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: The 730 accepted optimizer observations are overwhelmingly large concatenations of aromatic and heteroaromatic regions. Their median size is 116 heavy atoms, with 17 perceived rings and 16 aromatic rings, versus 31 heavy atoms and four perceived/aromatic rings for the complete Parent stream. All Child optimizer strings contain ring closures and aromatic atoms. Each observed seed leader has 119 heavy atoms. Seed 0 combines azaaromatic/coumarin-like carbonyl rings, nitriles, aryl thioethers, vinyl sulfides, ethers and halogenated linkers; seeds 1 and 2 repeatedly combine nitrogen-rich dione/aryl units with azaaromatic, nitrile and carbonyl regions. Such molecules contain familiar substructures but whole-molecule size, repeated modules and densely substituted connectivity make them far removed from ordinary small-molecule medicinal chemistry. Parent leaders instead have 30, 36 and 28 heavy atoms. The Child final records remain huge aromatic assemblies at evaluation 300, or at the censored evaluation 190/270 stops.
liabilities: The observed leaders combine extensive aromatic surface with numerous linked ring units; the seed-0 leader has RDKit molecular weight about 1667.27 Da. Solubility, conformational accessibility and synthesis were not measured.

Large heteroatom-rich assemblies coexist with vinyl-sulfide/halogenated-ether or unusual nitrogen linkages. The Parent also has O-F, S-Br or nitroso liabilities, so its higher labels do not certify clean chemistry.
Seeds 1 and 2 are terminally censored. Their absent late molecules and endpoints cannot be inferred, and the chemical size observation alone does not explain their timeout.
missing_features: Efficient compact realizations of the heterocyclic/polar arrangement seen in the stronger Parent are missing from the Child leading set. Abundant aromaticity, rings and nitrogen therefore do not diagnose the unmet chemistry.
Whole-molecule structural economy and chemically independent compact alternatives are poorly represented; adding a named target motif or inferring unobserved future molecules is unsupported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best initial fused aryl dione is 0.548381482770623. Child seed 0 reaches 0.6131669284924652 at evaluation 271; the observed seed-1 and seed-2 incumbents are 0.5851216343353792 at 185 and 0.6021671826625388 at 224. The low optimizer example at seed 2 evaluation 14 is already a large joined dione/amide framework and scores 0.5354820364463566. Within the Child stream larger related aromatic assemblies can have higher labels, but this does not establish a reward for size in general. The complete Parent reaches 0.8561477222467935 at seed 0 evaluation 281 with a compact linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione system. Particular arrangements of heteroaromatic and polar regions outperform indiscriminate repetition in this record; which exact objective feature is absent cannot be isolated from these adaptive histories.

per_task.generated_character: All 870 accepted optimizer strings contain halogens; nearly all contain aromatic atoms and ring closures. Median size is 74 heavy atoms and eight perceived rings, versus Parent 29 and four. Seed 0 concentrates on oversized halogenated aryl/N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine assemblies with enol, hydroxylamine and hydroperoxide appendages. Its best has 60 heavy atoms. Seed 1 contracts toward a 31-heavy-atom halogenated azaaryl system bearing a bridged/spiro small-ring tertiary arylamine and a fused aryl ether; the leader has eight perceived rings. Seed 2 reaches a 29-heavy-atom chlorinated biphenyl with phenol, enol/alkenyl substituents and a thiol-containing chain but no nitrogen. Thus nitrogen is not absent from the entire generator, and the best observed chemistry is highly seed-dependent. Parent leaders are smaller aryl-linked saturated amine systems with available aliphatic nitrogens. The Child final seed-0 product still carries peroxide/N-O functionality, seed 1 retains its crowded polycyclic arylamine, and seed 2 remains a substituted biaryl/azaaryl sulfur-chain series.
liabilities: Excessive aromatic/halogenated elaboration and multiple reactive appendages coexist. An O-O bond occurs in 109 of 870 Child optimizer observations, versus eight of 870 Parent observations.
The seed-1 leader has dense three-/four-membered and bridged connectivity with unassigned stereocentres. Parsing it does not establish feasible three-dimensional geometry.
The seed-0 leader exceeds 1000 Da by RDKit molecular weight and carries hydroperoxide/N-O chemistry; its label should not be read as medicinal-chemistry quality.
missing_features: Compact aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangements comparable to the stronger Parent are not reliably recovered. The Child can emit amines, but seed 0 often leaves nitrogen in sulfonyl/amide environments, seed 1 couples an arylamine to crowded small rings, and the seed-2 leader has none.

Chemically accessible alternatives retaining the useful spatial relationship between aromatic and polar regions are poorly represented; protonation, stereochemistry and conformations are not established by neutral graph notation.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
